newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid prices flat amid lower oil, natgas.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid prices flat amid lower oil, natgas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished the week mostly flat from Thursday's values amid lower crude oil prices and softer swing natural gas quotes in the cash market.
The New York Power Authority (NYPA) today broke recent spot inactivity from East Coast electric utilities.
It issued a tender due Monday for 100,000 barrels of 0.3 percent sulphur high-pour No 6 fuel grade for delivery between December 27-31 to its Astoria, N.Y., facility.
NYPA's solicitation failed to spark the New York harbor resid market.
"The East Coast is not really that cold yet," said a Houston trader in explaining the lack of price movement.
New York Harbor one pct remained in $21.75-22.00 a barrel range, with January paper was assessed at $21.75-$22.00, near unchanged from $21.80-$22.00 Thursday.
High sulphurs in New York market held steady, with 2.2 percent still near $18.13. NYH 0.3 percent high pour grade stayed in the $23.00 area.

U.S. Gulf Coast one percent grade firmed to $18.63 up from Thursday's $18.50, while three percent was steady at $15.50-$16.00. January three pct paper inched higher to $16.50-$16.85, up from Thursday's 16.00-$16.50.
New York city gate gas prices slipped to $4.90-$5.00/mmBtu from Thursday's $5.05 and compared with NYH one percent resid at a $3.47/mmBtu equivalent.
